title: Critique: Total Mutual Matches Metric
scenario: The BooedUp product team wants to measure whether a new AI Type Score model improves match quality. A stakeholder proposes tracking 'Total Mutual Matches per Week' as the primary success metric.
prompt: A stakeholder proposes using 'Total Mutual Matches per Week' to evaluate whether the new Type Score model is better than the baseline model. The team will A/B test the two models and compare weekly mutual match totals between the control and treatment groups. What is wrong with this metric? How would you fix it?
instructions: One short sentence: name the flaw, propose a fix. Aim for under 20 words total.
reference_answer: Should be normalized per active user. Mutual Match Rate (matches per active user per week) is better.

grading_rubric.description: Answer explicitly states the metric is not normalized or that cohort sizes may differ, making raw counts incomparable
Answer suggests a per-user or per-interaction denominator (e.g., matches per active user, matches per interaction initiated)
Answer provides a specific metric name (e.g., Mutual Match Rate, matches per MAU) rather than just saying 'use a rate'

hints: Think about whether you can compare raw counts across experiment groups.
What if the treatment group has more active users than the control group?
Consider what denominator would make the metric comparable even if cohort sizes differ.
common_mistakes: Suggesting a time-based normalization (per day vs per week) instead of per-subject normalization
Proposing a different count metric (e.g., total interactions) rather than a rate
Critiquing the choice of mutual matches as the outcome rather than the normalization flaw
Suggesting segmentation or filtering instead of fixing the denominator
